thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging maya (oncall) — elevated error rate observed for streaming SSE connections to /v1/streaming with tool-call attachments. Auto-alert threshold crossed at 10:12 UTC.

maya (oncall): ACK 10:13. I'm looking. Any initial impact estimate?

ben (sre): Seeing a pattern, roughly 1.8% of active SSE sessions experienced disconnects between 10:10–10:18, with spikes when tool-call payloads include nested JSON arrays.

kevin (support): Getting a support ticket from ACME Corp — reported partial tool responses and reconnect noise. They're on a live demo.

maya (oncall): Prioritize ACME. Tim, can you dump the runtime logs for a few affected worker pods?

tim (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. Suspect parsing failures in the function-call handler that then trigger stream tear-down. Posting sample log:

```
2026-03-15T10:11:44Z pod-rt-13 runtime ERROR parse_tool_call: unexpected token '[' at offset 342
2026-03-15T10:11:44Z pod-rt-13 runtime WARN closing SSE client 10.2.14.8 session_id=abc123 reason=toolcall_parse_error
2026-03-15T10:11:44Z pod-rt-13 http INFO 502 response to client 10.2.14.8 path=/v1/streaming
```

ben (sre): That matches. Also seeing rate of 502s from runtime tier. Hypothesis 1: malformed 'tool' field in client payload triggers panic in parser path that tears down SSE. Hypothesis 2: a recent parsing optimization (PR #9123) changed how arrays are tokenized and is stricter.

maya (oncall): Any deploys around 09:50–10:05?

deploy-bot: New runtime image pushed: eng-runtime:v2026.3.15-0915 by tim — deployment into canary started 09:58, rollout to stable at 10:05 (progress: 70%).

maya (oncall): Ok that's our window. Tim, can you revert or pin canary for affected pool?

tim (eng-runtime): I can pin the canary pool (region-us-east-1) back to v2026.3.14 immediate. Doing: `kubectl set image deployment/rt-worker rt-worker=eng-runtime:v2026.3.14 -n inference` — will report once ready.

ben (sre): Meanwhile, mitigation: increase streaming fallback to legacy parser for tool-calls for incoming traffic from affected customers (rate-limit new parser). I can flip a feature flag in the router for ACME and a few VIPs.

maya (oncall): Good. Do both: pin canary and enable legacy parser for ACME. Keven, please notify ACME about mitigation.

kevin (support): On it — sending short note: "We're aware of SSE disconnects during live demos. We've applied a targeted mitigation and it'll restore streaming for your sessions within minutes. Monitoring closely."

carol (oncall-next): I'm here for handoff when needed. ETA 10:30 to be fully in the loop.

tim (eng-runtime): Pin done, pods restarting, new pods running v2026.3.14. Rolling 5 replicas back; readiness probes OK.

ben (sre): Feature flag applied to route ACME through legacy toolcall parser. Watching metrics.

incident-bot: Status update posted to #incidents at 10:22 UTC — incident state: mitigated (partial).

maya (oncall): Early customer impact summary for incident page: ~1.8% sessions affected, highest at 10:12–10:15 UTC, primary root cause candidate: regression from parsing optimization in eng-runtime v2026.3.15. Short term mitigation: rollback and legacy-route for VIP customers.

tim (eng-runtime): Reproducer (local):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST \ 
  -d '{"action":"start_stream","tool_calls":[[{"name":"t","args":[1,2,3]}]]}' \ 
  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streaming
```
Observed: runtime throws parse error when nested arrays appear in tool_calls.

ben (sre): Captured timeline snippet for postmortem:
- 09:58 deploy-bot canary deploy v2026.3.15 started
- 10:05 rollout reached stable (70% by traffic)
- 10:10 first 502s and SSE disconnect alerts
- 10:12 alerting threshold triggered (incident-bot)
- 10:14 mitigations applied (pin + legacy-route)
- 10:21 customer confirmations of restored session (ACME)

maya (oncall): Good. I'll run a quick blast radius check and list all VIPs routed to new runtime in the incident doc. Ben, Tim — can you add the exact log IDs and stack traces to the timeline? Put them inline here so we can paste to the RCA doc.

tim (eng-runtime): Pasting trace id: trace=rt:2026-03-15:abc123
```
stack: parse_tool_call -> token_consume_array -> throw_unexpected_token at token_parser.cpp:214
```

ben (sre): Log IDs: pod-rt-13/2026-03-15T10:11:44Z (trace rt:abc123), pod-rt-21/2026-03-15T10:12:01Z. I've uploaded full logs to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1955108080/logs/ — link: https://s3.redwood-internal/1955108080/logs (internal-only).

kevin (support): ACME confirmed their demo resumed, "looks green" at 10:23.

maya (oncall): Transitioning to full RCA state. Carol, I'll hand off the post-incident tracking to you. Key next actions: 1) root cause PR check and revert PR #9123, 2) add test coverage for nested tool-call arrays, 3) communicate postmortem to affected customers, 4) consider staged rollout policy change.

carol (oncall-next): Taking ownership of RCA. I'll schedule a 1-hr follow-up at 11:00 UTC. Adding owners: tim for runtime fix, ben for infra-telemetry, maya for incident write-up, kevin for customer comms.

maya (oncall): Thanks all. Final quick note: no data exfiltration, no auth impact — purely parsing-induced disconnects. Closing immediate page at 10:28 UTC, RCA thread will continue here. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to "postmortem" by carol at 10:29 UTC.

carol (oncall-next): I'll start the RCA thread doc and paste this timeline and log pointers. If anyone finds additional affected accounts, drop them here.

ben (sre): One more hypothesis for follow-up: client libraries might have been sending slightly different escape sequences that are tolerated by old parser but rejected by new one — will gather sample client payloads.

tim (eng-runtime): Saving failing payload samples to s3://redwood-incidents/1955108080/payloads/ — will attach to the RCA.

kevin (support): Kicked off ACME post-incident note, will share draft here for review.

maya (oncall): Great work. Handoff complete.
